findings.claim: In all 4 activities the Your task heading is an h3 at the head of the workspace card but before that card's own h2 (the visually prefixed "Workspace: <step title>" heading). The outline therefore nests Your task and What success looks like under the reading-column step h2, and a learner moving by level-2 heading from the step heading to the workspace lands below the task and its success criteria. DESIGN.md's layout wireframe opens the workspace region with "h2 Your task", and its Typography table puts step h2s in both regions. Verified in JS-disabled Chromium on every activity. This dates from commit 2f281e85, which moved the task into the workspace, and was raised as a sub-point of edu-loop3-syntax-001; d3715dcd did not change it, so it is not a regression of that commit. Low: visual and DOM reading order are coherent, the task text is unchanged, and heading-navigation users still reach the task as an h3.
findings.recommendation: Place the workspace heading before the task block, or make Your task the workspace region's h2, so heading navigation reaches the task first and the outline matches the DESIGN.md wireframe.

findings.claim: The recap disclosure "Activity procedures (text alternative)" repeats every activity's steps as 4 consecutive ordered lists, each labelled only "Steps" with no activity name. d3715dcd copied the corrected in-activity wording into these lists, so the first list's first item now says the code is directly below these steps inside this same workspace, and the last list's says the question and code are in this workspace below these steps. That is true inside each activity, but in the recap copy no workspace or code follows; the next thing below is another unlabeled list. The artifact.md companion carries the same wording. A learner working from this text alternative is pointed at a place that does not exist where they are reading and cannot tell from the copy which activity it belongs to. Low: the in-activity steps are correct, and the code is reachable through the activities.
findings.recommendation: In the recap and Markdown copies, label each list with its activity name and phrase the location relative to that activity (for example, in that activity's workspace, below its task), instead of "these steps" and "this same workspace".

findings.claim: The recap message for an incomplete page has one wording for every incomplete state: it says that N activities settled without passing, asks the learner to review the explanations above, and says that to finish they should reload the page and work through it again. Two problems. First, after Restart activity on a passed activity, which with d3715dcd now correctly leaves page completion false, the learner can continue to the recap without re-passing it; that activity was restarted, not settled, so the count and the word settled are wrong. Second, for any incomplete state the reload advice contradicts the page's own settled feedback, which tells the learner to choose Restart activity to try again for credit; the page keeps no stored state, so a reload discards every other activity's progress when the timeline and Restart activity are the cheaper route. "Above" also points into the recap, where the activity explanations are not shown. Observed in JS-enabled Chromium after the committed public route: Restart of activity 2 and Continue to the recap gave data-pep-complete=false with this wording. The wording predates d3715dcd (it dates from d9019be2); d3715dcd only made the restarted path an honest incomplete state. Low: completion state and credit are correct, and only the guidance is misleading.
findings.recommendation: Count activities that are not passed rather than settled, and point the learner to the timeline and Restart activity on the named activities (for example, go back to the activity that is not passed and pass it, or choose Restart activity there) instead of reloading the page.

findings.claim: The new print rule shows the hidden recap section but hides its entire workspace until the learner reaches the recap. That workspace holds the recap model figure (line 715, a recap summary table) as well as the completion status lines. Printing from the recap prints the figure, so printed teaching now depends on where the learner prints: from any earlier activity the figure is omitted. On this page its Java-to-Python mapping table exists only in the recap, and 4 of its 15 cell parts use wording found nowhere else on the page. Reproduced in JS-enabled Chromium with print media emulated from activity 1 (figure not rendered) and, after running the committed public route to the recap, from the recap itself (figure rendered). Low: the concepts are taught in the activities, and the omission affects only pre-recap printing.
findings.recommendation: Print the recap model figure before the recap is reached as well, while keeping the not-yet-true completion lines ("All activities finished." and the completion message) out of pre-completion print, for example by hiding only the recap ask region instead of the whole workspace, after confirming the figure discloses nothing that answers a check the learner has not yet attempted.

The deliberate choice to keep the recap workspace out of print until the recap is reached also drops the recap model figure, which prints from the recap itself; that narrower gap is filed as edu-loop4-syntax-004 rather than reopening this id.
